title: Fix: Stock Detail chart legend click-to-toggle (analytic overlay lines) does not actually work
description:
User-reported bug: on the Stock Detail page, clicking an analytic overlay's legend label (e.g. the Fibonacci retracement lines, the channel/value-zone band, support/resistance zones, etc.) is supposed to toggle that line/overlay's visibility on the chart, but in practice it does not work. This feature was already built once -- `frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay` (PR #374) added a `LegendToggle` common component wired into 11 overlays across `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart`/`VolumeIndicatorsChart`/`TrendStrengthChart`, and two follow-up PRs (#376, #378) refined it further (shared `useSeriesVisibilityToggle` hook, now living in `utils/chart.ts`). Every one of those three PRs' own review records claims extensive verification including real-browser Playwright walkthroughs confirming toggles worked, mutation-tested hooks, and 99%+ test coverage -- `git log`/the code both confirm nothing has touched these files since PR #378 merged (2026-10-02), so this is either (a) a genuine regression from something else entirely (a shared dependency, a Lightweight Charts version bump, a React/MUI upgrade, a build/bundling change) that the previous reviews' live walkthroughs can no longer be assumed to reflect, (b) a real bug that slipped through all three rounds of review despite their own claims, or (c) a narrower case the previous task's scope never covered (recall `frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay`'s own decisions entry deliberately deferred False Breakout/Divergence/Kangaroo-Tail/price-chart marker-based overlays to a follow-up that was apparently never filed or never completed -- check `index.json` for any task matching that gap before assuming it's (a) or (b)). Do not assume any one of these going in -- this is a genuine investigation task, not a pre-diagnosed fix.

**The user has explicitly called out that a real test must be performed** -- not just unit tests with mocked Lightweight Charts series, which is exactly the kind of test the three merged PRs already had in abundance without catching whatever is currently broken. This task's own QA pass (and any PR built from it) needs an actual live browser walkthrough against a real running dev stack (`make dev` or equivalent, per `docs/architecture/Testing.md`/the `run` skill) clicking real legend rows on a real rendered chart and confirming the series genuinely appears/disappears on screen -- screenshots or an equivalent durable artifact, not just a passing vitest assertion against a mocked `series.applyOptions` call.

checklist.step: Reproduce the bug live: start the real dev stack (backend + frontend, fixture or real data provider), open the Stock Detail page for a ticker with multiple visible overlays, and click through every legend row across all four chart panes (PriceChart's Channel/Value Zone/Tide Background/Support-Resistance Zones/Fibonacci Retracement; OscillatorChart's RSI; VolumeIndicatorsChart's OBV/A-D; TrendStrengthChart's +DI/-DI/ADX/ATR). For each, confirm with a screenshot (or equivalent) whether clicking it actually (a) dims the legend row and (b) hides/shows the corresponding line/series/price-line on the chart. Record precisely which rows are broken versus working -- it may not be all-or-nothing.

Identify the actual root cause by reading the current code directly (don't stop at a plausible theory) -- check `LegendToggle.tsx`, `useSeriesVisibilityToggle` in `utils/chart.ts`, and each affected chart component's wiring. Consider dependency versions (`frontend/package.json`'s `lightweight-charts`/React/MUI versions versus what the original PRs tested against), browser console errors/warnings during a real click, and whether the bug reproduces in every browser or only specific conditions (e.g. after a range/interval change, after a ticker switch, only on certain overlay types).

Fix the identified root cause(s). If multiple independent causes are found across different overlay types, fix all of them in this task rather than leaving some broken. Record the diagnosis and fix rationale as a `decisions` entry, including what was ruled out and why -- per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement.
Add or update a genuine regression test that would have caught this (mutation-test it: temporarily reintroduce the bug, confirm the test fails, then restore the fix).

Perform a real browser walkthrough (not just the automated test suite) re-verifying every one of the 11 originally in-scope toggle targets actually works end to end on a live running app, with screenshots or an equivalent durable artifact as evidence -- this is the user's own explicit requirement for this task, not optional polish.

decisions.decision: Investigated exhaustively before concluding anything, per this task's own instruction not to pre-diagnose: ran a real Chromium dev stack (fixture data provider) and clicked every one of the 11 originally-in-scope toggle targets (Channel, Value Zone, Tide Background, Support/Resistance Zones, Fibonacci Retracement, RSI, OBV, A/D, +DI/-DI, ADX, ATR) across AAPL/MSFT, confirming via `aria-pressed`, computed `opacity`, and before/after screenshots that each one's legend dimming AND the actual chart series/price-line visibility both worked correctly -- in the dev server (`yarn dev`, React StrictMode active) AND a production build (`yarn build && vite preview`, StrictMode inactive, proxied to the real backend via a throwaway `vite.preview.temp.config.ts`, not committed), across a range switch (1Y->3M->1Y), an interval switch (Daily->Weekly->Daily), and an in-page ticker switch (AAPL->MSFT). All 11 worked in every one of these conditions -- no regression found anywhere in the originally-built feature, contradicting the user's own bug-report wording, which named Fibonacci/channel-value-zone/support-resistance-zones specifically as broken. Ruled out theory (a) (dependency drift): `git log -- frontend/package.json frontend/yarn.lock` shows no commit since well before PR #374 (the last touch was the Yarn-Berry migration, #116/#141) -- lightweight-charts/React/MUI versions are unchanged from what the three merged PRs' own reviews tested against. Also chased and ruled out a false lead: a Playwright test script of my own first appeared to show a ~960px unwanted `window.scrollY` jump specifically when toggling Accumulation/Distribution off after first toggling RSI and OBV in sequence -- confirmed via a native `window.addEventListener('scroll', ...)` + monkey-patched `scrollTo`/`scrollIntoView` that no in-app JS call caused it, then confirmed definitively it was a Playwright `locator.click()` actionability auto-scroll artifact of my own ad hoc test script (not the app) by dispatching a pure `element.click()` via `page.evaluate` instead, which showed zero scrollY change across the identical sequence -- not a real bug, not filed as a finding.
decisions.rationale: The task explicitly required ruling out (a)/(b) with real evidence before accepting (c) (a narrower, never-filed scope gap) as the answer, and explicitly warned against a pre-diagnosed theory -- a less careful pass could easily have reported the scroll-jump artifact as 'the bug' (it reproduced 100% of the time under my own initial unguarded script) without the extra step of dispatching a pure JS click to isolate test-tooling behavior from app behavior. Running both a dev AND a production build matters specifically because this codebase's `main.tsx` wraps the app in `React.StrictMode`, whose dev-only double-invoked effects could in principle mask a real effect-ordering bug that only manifests with StrictMode off (production) -- confirming identical, correct behavior in both rules that out as a contributing factor too.

decisions.decision: Root cause: theory (c), exactly as this task's own description flagged as a possibility to check first -- `frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay`'s own `decisions` entry deliberately deferred click-to-toggle for 4 legend rows (PriceChart's False Breakout, Divergence, and Kangaroo Tail; OscillatorChart's own separate Divergence row) because each is drawn via `createSeriesMarkers`/`series.createPriceLine` (no `visible` option on either, confirmed by reading `lightweight-charts`' own `.d.ts`), a materially different toggle mechanism than the `applyOptions({ visible })` used by the 11 series-backed overlays -- and a follow-up task to give them the same affordance was 'apparently never filed or never completed' (confirmed: grepped `docs/tasks/index.json` for every divergence/kangaroo-tail/false-breakout/legend/toggle id -- no such follow-up exists; `frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay-followups`/`-followups-followups` both addressed only a dimming-opacity constant and a hook's file placement, neither touched these 4 rows). Confirmed live via DOM inspection (`querySelectorAll('button')` vs. the plain-text swatch+label+MetricHelp `Stack` rows) that all 4 of these rows render with ZERO click affordance of any kind prior to this fix -- no `role="button"`, no `cursor: pointer`, no dimming on click, nothing -- while sitting in the exact same `Stack` layout, with the exact same swatch+caption+MetricHelp shape, directly alongside rows that ARE click-to-toggle (e.g. False Breakout is the second row in the same `Stack` as the now-toggleable Support/Resistance Zones). A user clicking one of these 4 rows -- which the task's own user-report cites generically ('e.g. ... support/resistance zones, etc.') rather than claiming to have tested literally only the 3 already-working examples named -- would reasonably perceive the whole 'click a legend label to toggle' feature as broken, with no visual cue distinguishing a toggleable row from an inert one anywhere on the page. Fixed by extending click-to-toggle to all 4 rows, using the same 'skip creation while hidden' mechanism this codebase's own Fibonacci-levels effect already established for `IPriceLine` (which has no `visible` option): False Breakout's marker+price-line creation was extracted out of the effect it previously shared with the Support/Resistance zone bands (so toggling it can't tear down/recreate those bands, the same z-order/collateral-redraw concern `channelSeriesRef`'s own doc comment already documents for series-backed overlays) into its own dedicated effect, redundantly recomputing `displayedZones`/`zoneRenderData` from the same `historyQuery.data`/`analysisQuery.data`/`theme` inputs (a deliberate, cheap duplication of pure computation, the same convention this component's own legend-text `displayedZones` const already uses to independently stay in sync with what the drawing effect draws); PriceChart's Divergence and Kangaroo Tail effects (already each independently isolated, with no sibling overlay to disturb) simply fold the new toggle boolean directly into their own existing gate/dependency array; OscillatorChart's own Divergence effect gets the identical treatment.
decisions.rationale: A ref + small dedicated `useSeriesVisibilityToggle`-style effect (the mechanism every series-backed overlay already uses) isn't available here since `ISeriesMarkersPluginApi`/`IPriceLine` both lack a `visible` option to apply -- `setMarkers([])`/remove-then-recreate would have worked too, but 'skip creation while hidden, folded into the effect's own gate' is simpler (no new ref-ownership bookkeeping across two effects, no question of which effect's cleanup is responsible for a price line the other effect created) and is already a proven, reviewed pattern in this exact file (Fibonacci). Extracting False Breakout into its own effect (rather than folding its toggle into the existing shared zone-bands effect's dependency array) specifically avoids tearing down and recreating the Support/Resistance zone `BaselineSeries` bands on every False-Breakout toggle click -- the same 'toggling one overlay has no reason to disturb an unrelated sibling overlay sharing an effect purely because of how the component happens to be organized' principle this file's own `channelSeriesRef` doc comment already establishes for the Channel/Value-Zone/EMA13-26 case, now extended to a marker/price-line overlay instead of a series. Divergence/Kangaroo Tail needed no such extraction since each was already its own independent effect with nothing else sharing it. Verified the `addSeries` call count for the Support/Resistance zone bands is genuinely unaffected by a False Breakout toggle (a dedicated assertion in the new regression test, `expect(addSeriesMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` across a full hide/show cycle) -- confirming the extraction achieved its purpose, not just that the toggle itself works.

decisions.decision: Visual composition when a toggled-off row is ALSO currently out of the visible bar range (a case this task's own description flagged as previously left undecided -- 'what does toggled off AND out of range look like together'): `LegendToggle`'s own `active`-driven opacity (dimming the WHOLE row, swatch+label, to `LEGEND_DIM_OPACITY` when toggled off) and each row's own pre-existing swatch-only 'not in current range' opacity (also `LEGEND_DIM_OPACITY`, applied only to the swatch `Box`, unchanged) are left as two independently-applied, naturally-stacking CSS `opacity` values rather than inventing any new composed state or suppressing one when the other is active. The '(not in current range)' text suffix and the swatch's own out-of-range dimming are left wrapped INSIDE `LegendToggle`'s children exactly as before (unchanged), so both signals keep firing independently of the toggle state -- a toggled-off-but-in-range row reads as single-dimmed (just the toggle); a toggled-off-and-out-of-range row reads as double-dimmed (toggle opacity wrapping an already-dimmed swatch, i.e. visibly more washed out, not a conflicting or broken-looking state); a toggled-ON-but-out-of-range row (the only case already possible before this fix) is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: This matches the exact precedent this component already established for Fibonacci's own 'still describe it, just don't draw it' legend text while toggled off (the swing/bar-count text keeps updating even while hidden) -- extended here to mean the out-of-range caveat ALSO keeps describing the real underlying state regardless of the user's own toggle preference, rather than one state masking the other. Rejected inventing a single combined 'super-dimmed' sentinel opacity value or suppressing the out-of-range suffix while toggled off: neither was asked for by this task's checklist (which only asked that SOME decision be made and recorded, not a specific one), and both would add a new state transition to reason about for zero behavioral benefit over simply letting two independent, already-existing opacity values compose the way CSS opacity naturally does when nested.

decisions.decision: Did not attempt to make Kangaroo Tail's toggle reachable via a live browser walkthrough (only via the mutation-tested unit test, same mechanism as False Breakout/Divergence, both of which WERE live-verified) -- confirmed by querying `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` directly against the fixture data provider that none of its 4 deterministic tickers (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA/GOOGL) ever produce a non-null `kangaroo_tail` at any range, a pre-existing limitation of `FixtureDataProvider`'s synthetic data generation, not something this task touches.
decisions.rationale: Modifying `FixtureDataProvider` to synthesize a Kangaroo Tail pattern is out of scope for a legend-toggle bug-fix task (a materially different, riskier change to shared test/dev infrastructure every other frontend task also depends on) and isn't necessary to be confident the fix is correct: Kangaroo Tail's new toggle effect is structurally identical to Divergence's and False Breakout's (same `createSeriesMarkers`/`createPriceLine` skip-while-hidden mechanism, same effect shape, same mutation-tested assertions), both of which were independently confirmed correct live against real rendered chart content (MSFT, `range=max`) with before/after screenshots. The unit test's own mutation test (reverting the gate and confirming the test fails) gives the same confidence the live walkthrough gives the other three, for the one case fixture data can't exercise end to end.

comments.summary: BLOCKING: PriceChart's and OscillatorChart's separate Divergence legend rows both now render a real <button> via LegendToggle with the identical accessible name 'Hide Divergence on the chart' / 'Show Divergence on the chart'. Both panes are always mounted together on the Stock Detail page (StockCharts.tsx) and both derive their divergence existence from the exact same `analysisQuery.data?.divergence` value, so both rows render simultaneously with identical names whenever a divergence exists and the oscillator pane is shown (the ordinary/common case, not a rare edge case) -- confirmed live myself (MSFT, max range, daily interval): both 'Divergence' toggle buttons are on-screen at once with the same aria-label. Before this PR neither row was interactive (plain Box/Typography, no role='button'), so this collision did not exist; this PR introduces it by giving both an identical, non-unique accessible name. This breaks basic accessible-naming uniqueness for screen-reader users (both announce identically, no way to tell which pane a given button controls) and breaks any `getByRole('button', { name: 'Hide Divergence on the chart' })`-style query run against the composed page without scoping to one pane's container -- I hit this exact strict-mode violation myself while writing an unscoped Playwright locator against the real running app, and had to scope every PriceChart query to its own pane specifically to work around it. Needs a disambiguating label per pane (e.g. passing the pane name into LegendToggle's label, 'Divergence (Price Chart)' vs 'Divergence (Oscillators)', or an equivalent fix) before this can be accepted. (Caught by the code-review skill's background pass, independently corroborated by my own hands-on testing.)

Non-blocking: the newly-extracted False Breakout effect calls buildZoneRenderData(...) purely to get at zone.false_breakout via zoneRenderData's .zone field, discarding the fillColor/lineColor/lineStyle it computes -- displayedZones already carries false_breakout directly, so the extra mapping (building unused color/line-style strings on every render of this effect, including every toggle click) is pure waste reintroduced by the extraction. A plain `for (const zone of displayedZones)` would do the same job without it. (Caught by the code-review skill's background pass.)

No persisted e2e spec (frontend/tests/e2e/*.spec.ts) covers the chart legend click-to-toggle feature at all -- not any of the 11 original toggles nor the 4 this PR adds. Non-blocking (make e2e's existing 27 specs all pass unaffected), but tracked as a follow-up since this exact category of gap -- a feature whose only prior verification was mocked unit tests plus an ad hoc, non-persisted walkthrough -- is part of why this bug went undetected through 3 earlier review rounds.
PR description states the frontend vitest suite passed 1037/1037; independently re-ran twice and got 1035/1035 (coverage percentages matched exactly). Non-blocking, a self-reported count nit only.

review.notes:
Full review of PR #391. Static analysis clean on both sides (backend ruff+mypy, frontend eslint+tsc -b --noEmit, profit-target wording guard). Backend pytest --cov: 1616 passed, 100% coverage (unaffected, frontend-only diff). Frontend yarn vitest run --coverage: 1035/1035 passed (see follow-up note on the PR's '1037' claim), statements 99.77%/branches 99.05%/functions 99.84%/lines 99.81% -- well above the 90% gate. Ran make e2e (full persisted Playwright suite): 27/27 specs passed.

Independently mutation-tested 2 of the 4 new toggle gates myself (reverted the `!kangarooTailVisible`/`!falseBreakoutVisible` gate, confirmed the corresponding new regression test fails, restored the fix, confirmed it passes again) -- matches the PR's own claimed mutation-testing methodology for all 4.

Performed my own independent real-Chromium walkthrough (not just trusting task-worker's own claimed walkthrough) against a freshly-started dev stack (fixture data provider, MSFT ticker, Max range) via a throwaway Playwright script (not committed): clicked all 11 originally-built toggles (Channel, Value Zone, Tide Background, Support/Resistance Zones, Fibonacci Retracement, RSI, OBV, A/D, +DI/-DI, ADX, ATR) plus 3 of the 4 newly-fixed rows reachable with fixture data (False Breakout, PriceChart's Divergence, OscillatorChart's own separate Divergence) -- every one genuinely showed/hid real chart content (price lines, markers, series, dotted trend lines) on click, confirmed via `aria-pressed` state transitions AND before/after-hide/after-show screenshots with differing pixel content (not just CSS opacity), with zero console/network errors attributable to the toggle clicks themselves. No regression found in the 11 original toggles, matching the PR's own claim. It was precisely this hands-on walkthrough (writing my own Playwright locators against the real composed page rather than only reading the PR's isolated-component unit tests) that surfaced the duplicate-accessible-name blocking finding below -- the per-component unit tests can't catch it since each test file mounts only one of the two components in isolation.

Independently verified the Kangaroo Tail live-walkthrough limitation is genuine, not a corner cut: queried the real fixture-mode backend's `/api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` directly across all 4 fixture tickers (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA/GOOGL) x 7 ranges (1m/3m/6m/1y/3y/5y/max) -- `kangaroo_tail` was null in every single case, confirming no fixture ticker/range combination can exercise this overlay live. The PR's reliance on its mutation-tested unit test alone for this one row is justified.

Independently confirmed the 'Object is disposed' console error observed during the walkthrough and during make e2e is pre-existing, not a regression from this PR: reproduced the identical error (same stack trace, same timing -- during initial chart mount, before any toggle interaction) against a `main`-branch worktree with no changes from this PR applied. Also cross-checked docs/tasks/done/frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay-followups-followups.json's own review notes, which already documented this exact message as pre-existing lightweight-charts/React-StrictMode chart-teardown-timing noise unrelated to that PR's diff -- same conclusion applies here.

Cross-checked the investigation's factual claims against the task board itself rather than trusting them at face value: confirmed docs/tasks/done/frontend-chart-legend-toggle-overlay.json's own decisions entry does deliberately defer exactly these 4 rows (False Breakout, PriceChart Divergence, OscillatorChart Divergence, Kangaroo Tail) for the stated reason (no `visible` option on `ISeriesMarkersPluginApi`/`IPriceLine`), and confirmed via index.json that no follow-up task to give them toggle affordance was ever filed before this one.

Ran the code-review skill (medium effort, backgrounded) against the diff; it returned two findings after this review's manual pass was otherwise complete -- one blocking (the duplicate accessible-name collision above, which I independently corroborated live), one non-blocking (the wasted buildZoneRenderData computation above). Both are included in comments; the blocking one is why this verdict is needs_work rather than accepted despite every other check (tests, coverage, static analysis, e2e, live walkthrough, methodology/decisions records) passing cleanly. Two of the four comments above are non-blocking and have also been filed as checklist items on frontend-chart-legend-toggle-not-working-followups per CLAUDE.md's tracked-follow-up rule; the duplicate-name finding is not filed there since it's blocking and belongs to the rework of this task itself, not a future follow-up.
